Subject: Follow-up from today — EU residency, retention & JIT support gating

Alex — thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap so we’re aligned and to make next steps explicit: 

• PII scope: data types that will flow to Redwood are customer names, email, and transaction metadata (no raw payment tokens). You confirmed EU customer records must remain in EU regions.
• Retention ask: NephroHealth wants 90-day short-term retention for logs/requests and the ability to request longer retention for audit windows.
• Support access: you require break-glass / JIT access for our support engineers with audit logs and an approval workflow owned by your Security team.
• RBAC: least-privilege model, separation between support and engineering, per-customer entitlement.

Attachments I’m sharing: nephro-data-handoff-template.xlsx (fields you can confirm), a draft EU deployment diagram, and a short RBAC proposal (ben is cc’d with the tech details).

Proposed next steps (please confirm):
1) Ben to provide a concise RBAC + break-glass runbook and retention policy options by EOD 11/08.
2) Security deep-dive with your Security lead next week (we suggested Thu 11/12 10:00 CET).
3) You to share any mandatory contractual language re: data residency/retention before the call.

If that looks right I’ll lock the HD call and drop a shared Drive link with our runbooks.

Marcus — thanks, that summary is accurate. A few clarifications from our side: 

• Residency: All records tied to EU customers must be stored and processed in EU zones. We are open to hosted EU offerings (not on-prem yet).
• Retention: 90 days for transactional logs is our default. For regulatory holds we need to be able to request preservation for up to 2 years; please confirm if that is a manual request or automated policy.
• Support access: Strong preference for a JIT workflow that requires both a NephroHealth security approver and a 1-hour auto-expiry. Every break-glass event must create an immutable audit entry and be exportable.
• Evidence: please send SOC 2 Type II report or equivalent and the network diagram (we need DC locations for legal).

I’ve looped in Daniel (security@nephrohealth.com) — Daniel will own the deep-dive scheduling. Thu 11/12 10:00 CET sounds OK but Daniel will confirm.

Date: 2026-11-08T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: RBAC + break-glass proposal (high level)

Alex / Marcus — following up with the technical outline Marcus promised. High level summary: 

1) RBAC model (recommended)
   - Tenant-scoped roles: support_readonly, support_elevated, infra_admin (Redwood internal).
   - Principle of least privilege: support_elevated is time-limited and scoped to a single tenant by default.

2) JIT / Break-glass workflow
   - Request initiated in Console with justification + ticket link.
   - Approval gate: NephroHealth security approver (SAML group) OR designated security mailbox.
   - Access granted for configurable TTL (default 60 minutes).
   - All sessions proxied through audit service; keystroke-level logs are out of scope, but API/console interactions are recorded.

3) Audit & retention
   - All break-glass events and support session traces are immutable and retained 365 days by default.
   - Logs are exportable in NDJSON/CSV for legal requests or e-discovery.

4) Residency + deployment
   - We can host completely in EU region (Frankfurt or Amsterdam) so no data leaves EU for supported tenants.
   - Optionally we can offer a dedicated VPC/pool for NephroHealth for stronger isolation (quote required).

Concrete asks from us to move forward:
• Alex / Daniel: confirm SSO provider + group that will approve JIT requests (IdP metadata if possible).
• NephroHealth legal: any mandatory retention triggers beyond standard holds.

I’ve attached a short RBAC proposal and a diagram showing the EU-hosting option. Happy to run the technical deep-dive next Thursday.

—
Ben Carter
Sr. Product Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com
